name: Arlington Memorial Bridge

name: Key Bridge
note: The roadway is a legal, ordinary climb, not barred - riders use it every day. sidepath_only marks it anyway: it is a narrow bridge with no shoulder and no way off mid-span, so a mass ride still has to be kept to the sidewalk provision rather than the traffic lane. Do not read sidepath_only as a legality claim; roadway_bicycle_legal is the legality claim. The DC-Virginia boundary on the Potomac is the 1791 Virginia shoreline, not the channel, so this span lies within the District along essentially its whole length and MPD's jurisdiction runs end to end - the same shape as the Arlington Memorial Bridge row, which is the right shape for every Potomac span. The earlier split down the middle was the midpoint heuristic written into the data. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge, not a legal statement. The Virginia approach ramps beyond the abutment are VDOT's and Arlington County's; the structure is not. Checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: inside this file's region the name reaches four highway=trunk ways, ref US 29, and nothing else; Baltimore's Francis Scott Key Bridge (I-695, the name in bridge:name) is the other structure of that name in the coverage area and is outside it. All four roadway ways carry bicycle=no and foot=no in that extract, so this row's roadway_bicycle_legal true is a claim against OSM's own tag, and the remap writes bicycle=yes over it.

name: George Mason Memorial Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This one carries I-395's southbound lanes out of the District, and it is where the shared-use path is: the Mount Vernon Trail connection that ramps to Columbia Island on the Virginia side and Ohio Drive SW on the District side is a sidewalk on this highway span, not a structure of its own and not on the Metro bridge. The roadway carries bicycle=no, so roadway_bicycle_legal is false; the path is the only and the intended crossing, so sidepath_only is true. Two claims here are community knowledge rather than record and they are not held at the same confidence. That this span is the one carrying the path is medium-high, from the reviewer who rides it, and it is the one claim a survey could move. The direction is medium-high too and was recorded backwards until round 5: the 1950 Williams span carries the northbound lanes into the District - it is the span Air Florida flight 90 struck - so this 1962 span carries the southbound lanes out of it. Names checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: two highway=motorway ways, ref I 395;US 1, bicycle=no, oneway and drawn from the District end toward Virginia, which agrees with the southbound direction above. Which span carries the path is not something that check can see.

name: Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial Bridge
osm_names: Arland D. Williams Junior Memorial Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This row said this was the Metrorail bridge and that it carried the Mount Vernon Trail connection. It is neither. It is the 1950 highway span carrying I-395's northbound lanes into the District - the one Air Florida flight 90 struck in January 1982, renamed in 1985 for the passenger who passed the rescue line to others and drowned. That it is the 1950 span and that it is the span flight 90 struck are matters of record, not OSM questions; which direction it carries is community knowledge at medium-high confidence and was recorded backwards until round 5, as southbound. The Metro crossing is the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge, a separate structure with its own row, and the shared-use path is on the George Mason Memorial Bridge. So this span is bicycle=no on the roadway with no sidepath on it: barred outright, not sidepath-only. The OSM spelling writes Junior out - "Arland D. Williams Junior Memorial Bridge" - so the row matched nothing until osm_names said so. On the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 that name is on six highway=motorway ways, ref I 395;US 1, bicycle=no, oneway and drawn from the Virginia end toward the District, which agrees with the northbound direction above; the direction is still community knowledge that the map happens to agree with.

name: Charles R. Fenwick Bridge
note: One of the five parallel structures at the 14th Street crossing, which this file used to record as three. The five are three highway spans - Arland D. Williams Jr. Memorial (1950), George Mason Memorial (1962), Rochambeau (1972) - plus the Long Bridge carrying freight and commuter rail and the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge carrying Metro's Yellow Line. Not one bridge and not one answer, which is why they are separate rows. This is the Metro crossing - the Yellow Line between Pentagon and L'Enfant Plaza - and it was missing from this file entirely while its name sat on the Williams row's note. A Metro bridge carries no roadway and no path: there is no bicycle access of any kind, which is why roadway_bicycle_legal is false and sidepath_only is false together. It is recorded so the structure has a row of its own rather than being rediscovered as somebody else's identity. The spelling is right and still cannot match: the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 carries "Charles R. Fenwick Bridge" in bridge:name on two railway=subway ways named Washington Metro - Yellow Line, and the pipeline reads highway ways only (extract.read_ways), so no rail way ever reaches the resolvers. The row reports itself unmatched on every rebuild for that reason rather than because the name is wrong, and osm_names_verified stays false because nothing the pipeline reads can confirm it.

name: Long Bridge
note: The fifth of the five structures at the 14th Street crossing, and the rail one: freight, and the commuter and intercity trains that share it. No roadway and no path. It has a row for exactly the reason the Charles R. Fenwick Bridge has one, and until round 5 it did not - this file stated a rule, "no row for anything rail-only", and then broke it for Fenwick one paragraph later. One rule for both: a structure at a crossing this deployment has an opinion about gets a row, whatever it carries, so that its identity is recorded here rather than rediscovered on somebody else's row. roadway_bicycle_legal and sidepath_only are false together, which is what "no bicycle access of any kind" looks like in these two columns. The name is the most collidable in this file - Arlington has a Long Bridge Park and a Long Bridge Drive - but the match is exact and restricted to bridge-tagged, non-trail-class ways, so a park path or a street named after the bridge is not reachable by it. Ownership is CSX's and row_owner_verified is false: the structure is CSX's, the trains on it are not all CSX's, and this file has not checked which entity holds the right-of-way at either abutment. Unmatched on the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 for two reasons at once: no way in it carries the name "Long Bridge", and the structure is rail, which the pipeline never reads (extract.read_ways keeps highway ways only). Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Woodrow Wilson Bridge path
police: Alexandria PD / Prince George's County Police / MPD
note: The roadway carries I-95/I-495 and bicycle=no in OSM; the shared-use path is a separate structure and the only crossing. Three authorities, not two: the Maryland end is in Prince George's County, and the span clips the District itself - the Wilson Bridge is the one Potomac crossing that touches all three - so MPD belongs here alongside Alexandria and Prince George's. row_owner was MDTA and is now MDOT SHA: MDTA is Maryland's toll authority and this bridge is toll-free, which is the tell; MDOT SHA operates it. Medium confidence, and row_owner_verified stays false - ownership of the connecting right-of-way on the Virginia side (the Jones Point sliver, the short-crossing case) may sit with VDOT again. The name this row claimed, "Woodrow Wilson Memorial Bridge", is on no way in the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24, so the row matched nothing. There the roadway is twenty highway=motorway ways, ref I 95;I 495, bicycle=no: the western ways named "Capital Beltway (Local)" and "Capital Beltway (Thru)" with bridge:name "Woodrow Wilson Bridge" and "Woodrow Wilson Bridge (Thru)", the eastern ways named "Woodrow Wilson Memorial Bridge (Local)", some with bridge:name "Woodrow Wilson Memorial Bridge (Thru)". Those four spellings are what osm_names claims. The path is separate highway=cycleway ways named "Woodrow Wilson Bridge" and "Woodrow Wilson Bridge Trail"; the first shares a spelling with the roadway's bridge:name, and the trail-class guard is what keeps this row off it. Names checked against that extract.

name: 11th Street Bridge (local span)

A bike-legal roadway with its own provision and a connection to the Anacostia Riverwalk Trail at either end, so it is neither barred nor sidepath-only: this is the row that makes the 11th Street crossing usable by a ride, and the one the old single row's values described. This row claimed the plain name "11th Street Bridge" as the local span's, and the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 has that name on exactly one way, which is not this span: bridge:name on way 546095934, highway=motorway, name Southeast Freeway, ref I 695 - a freeway span, where this row's true landed. The claim is removed, so the row now matches on its own label, which no way carries, and reports itself unmatched. The candidates for the local span in that extract are four bridge ways named "11th Street Southeast", highway=secondary, one about 270 m long beside the freeway span and three short ones at its south end, and every one of them carries bicycle=no and foot=no. Claiming that name would put this row's true on all four and write bicycle=yes over OSM's bicycle=no on each, so it is not claimed: which way is the span, and whether this row's legality claim should stand against that tag, are for a reviewer to settle. Community working knowledge, unverified against a real extract.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Bridge
note: Carries I-66 and US-50 across the Potomac, with no sidepath on the structure, so this is barred outright rather than sidepath-only. This note said the bridge was tagged highway=trunk, which MOTOR_ONLY does not catch, so that the no-trail variant depended entirely on the rm:bridge_bicycle mechanism to keep a mass ride off it; it also said bicycle=no in OSM. The Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24 disproves both: OSM names the structure "Theodore Roosevelt Memorial Bridge" - which is why this row matched nothing until osm_names said so - and all seventeen of its bridge ways are highway=motorway, refs I 66, US 50 and I 66;US 50, with no bicycle tag at all. Highway class keeps a ride off it, and this row's false agrees with that rather than standing alone. Names checked against that extract; the authority columns remain community working knowledge.

name: American Legion Bridge
police: Montgomery County Police / Maryland State Police
note: Carries the Capital Beltway (I-495) across the Potomac near Cabin John. No bicycle or pedestrian provision of any kind - not sidepath-only, no access. The police column was a split down the middle, Montgomery County and Fairfax County, which is the midpoint heuristic this file exists to override, written into the data. The shoreline reasoning that puts every District span under one authority applies here with the line in a different place: above Washington the Potomac is Maryland's to the Virginia bank, which Virginia v. Maryland (2003) left undisturbed as to the boundary itself while deciding what Virginia may do from its own shore, so this span lies essentially in Maryland along its whole length. Montgomery County Police and the Maryland State Police, then, with Fairfax County reached only at the Virginia approach beyond the abutment - the same shape the Key Bridge row gives VDOT and Arlington County. Boundary is a matter of record; the policing that follows from it is community working knowledge at medium confidence, not a legal statement. row_owner reads MDOT SHA rather than "Maryland SHA", which is the same agency under a spelling this file no longer uses. The alias "George Kennan Memorial Bridge" has been removed: nothing places that name on this structure or on any other crossing in the coverage area, and an unplaceable alias in this file is a name that can only ever match the wrong way. Names checked against the Geofabrik DC+MD+VA extract of 2026-09-24: the bridge:name is on the two highway=motorway ways of the Capital Beltway, ref I 495, bicycle=no, one each way. The authority columns remain community working knowledge.
